title: I’ve finished everything I planned for the game. What’s next, and is it worth it? :)
author: Best-Improvement1745
selftext:
About four months ago, I shared the first version of my Minigolf game here, which was inspired by Gravity Defied, Bounce, and Worms. To acquire players, I used Meta targeted ads, which brought in a small audience. At that time, the game had around 20 levels. After that, I gradually added level after level, sent push notifications about updates to players, and step-by-step brought the total number of free levels up to 40. Throughout this period, the game maintained a low but stable level of activity (roughly 10–20 daily active users).  
Next, I sat down to develop a separate pack of 20 paid levels to test in practice whether people would be willing to pay for the game (spoiler: so far, nobody is willing to :)). Since I was working on the entire pack at once, no updates were released for a bit over a month; however, activity in the game still remained at that low yet steady level.  
So, given these numbers and data, what would you advise doing next?  
P.S. During the targeted ad campaign, D1 retention was around 25%. I don't recall D7, but it was extremely low.

comments.author: fued
comments.body:
release for free and start the next game.

looks like a good learning experience, but not sure its good enough to sell sorry

comments.author: melty_program
comments.body: How many players have finished the 40 free levels and actually seen the paid pack? With 10–20 daily players, zero purchases could mean hardly anyone has reached it yet. I'd check that before building more levels or concluding people won't pay. If most drop off well before that point, watching a few first sessions might be more useful than another content update.

replies.author: Best-Improvement1745
replies.body: Not much, around 9% reach 40 level. Thank you!

replies.author: melty_program
replies.body: Thanks for checking! With 9% reaching level 40, I'd want to know how many actually saw the paid pack before judging demand for it. Do you track where players stop in the free levels? A big drop at one level would suggest a different next step from a gradual decline throughout.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
Cool prototype but this art style looks shit on a tiny screen, and probably also on a large screen.

Anyway since you care more about paid ads and retention than game design, I'll just shut up.

replies.author: Best-Improvement1745
replies.body: I’d be interested to hear some advices on design

replies.body: Son unos bichos extraterrestres que van rodando, es un ejemplo de en que podrías enfocar el diseño
